pulls.title: 8395819: RISC-V: Implement compact uncommon trap sequences
pulls.author: DingliZhang
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, please consider. This change enables compact C2 uncommon traps on RISC-V using `MachUncommonTrapNode`, following [JDK-8393085](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8393085). The current static Java call representation introduces register spills and post-call nops. Preserving live registers in the uncommon trap blob reduces the code needed at trap sites. The RISC-V sequence consists of an `AUIPC/JALR` pair followed by a 32-bit trap request. The register saver is shared with the deoptimization code, and the existing call-based uncommon-trap test configurations are enabled for RISC-V. ### Test

pulls.author: DingliZhang
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, please consider. The RISC-V C2 backend currently has no matching rule for `VectorSlice`. The IR byte offset is converted to a lane offset, and the slice is implemented using `vslidedown` and `vslideup`. pulls.body_excerpt: When Shenandoah performs a full GC, `-XX:+HeapDumpBeforeFullGC` and `-XX:+HeapDumpAfterFullGC` crash the VM. pulls.title: 8307970: Thread.start is slow with large number of threads
pulls.author: fbredber
pulls.body_excerpt: This PR reduces the Thread-SMR (Safe Memory Reclamation) related cost of starting and exiting threads. Both starting and exiting a thread create a new `ThreadsList` and retire the old one. Previously, we used to scan the hazard pointers of all threads when a `ThreadsList` was retired. This made the execution cost increasingly higher as more threads were started. This PR tackles the problem in three ways: 1. By not scanning hazard pointers every time a new thread is started. Instead, we defer the scanning until either 16 `ThreadsLists` have been retired or the retired lists occupy at least 4 MB

pulls.title: 8393068: Optimize uniform vector byte shift operations using x86 GFNI instruction
pulls.author: jatin-bhateja
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi All, x86 AVX-512 targets provides packed shifts for 16, 32, and 64-bit lanes, but not for bytes. C2 lowers LShiftVB, RShiftVB, and URShiftVB by widening bytes to words, shifting, masking, and packing. That sequence is the byte-shift bottleneck. GFNI **gf2p8affineqb** instruction applies one 8×8 bit matrix to every byte. Logical left, logical right, and arithmetic right shifts by 0..7 are fixed matrices derived from the identity 0x0102040810204080. pulls.title: 8377154: AArch64: Merging SIMD ld/st into ldp/stp in macro-assembler
pulls.author: fg1417
pulls.body_excerpt: JDK-8196064 added support for merging 4- and 8-byte scalar load/store operations into load/store pairs. The AArch64 platform also supports SIMD load/store pairs for SIMD&FP registers[1]. This patch extends that functionality to support merging 4-, 8-, and 16-byte vector load/store operations into vector load/store pairs. For example, given the following assembly: ``` str q16, [x14, #32] str q16, [x14, #48] ``` after this change, it can be merged into: ``` stp q16, q16, [x14, #32] ``` Tier 1~3 tests passed on aarch64 platform. pulls.title: 8336759: C2: int counted loop with long limit not recognized as counted loop
pulls.author: tabjy
pulls.body_excerpt: This patch implements [JDK-8336759](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8336759) that recognizes int counted loops with long limits. Currently, patterns like `for ( int i =...; i < long_limit; ...)` where int `i` is implicitly promoted to long (i.e., `(long) i < long_limit`) is not recognized as (int) counted loop. This patch speculatively and optimistically converts long limits to ints and deoptimize if the limit is outside int range, allowing more optimization opportunities.
